new.n: Danish recluse Lars Nielson's $10,000-13,000 hidden on his farm, sec 14 Morken Township
new.pl: Nielson's 320 acres in sec 14 T141N R47W, Morken Twp (Clay Co.); the half section and the sod-shanty site are not yet read off a plat
new.st: Lars Nielson, a Danish recluse, held 320 acres in sec 14 of Morken Township for about 36 years and died 30 Sep 1916, aged 75, with no heirs. He never had a bank account and demanded gold certificates for his grain. Neighbors put his hidden money at $10,000-11,000 at least, later $13,000 in gold, silver and currency. Only a dusty $10 bill was found in the house (built about 1912, no cellar). His original sod shanty stood 32 years, and its site was thought the likeliest spot. The administrator had the farm searched systematically and found nothing. By Aug 1919 diggers came at night to the old shack used as a barn and to the shanty site. No recovery was reported.
new.t: Search the sod-shanty site and the old shack/barn; the 1912 house had no cellar. Find the sites on a Clay Co. plat and the 1939 aerial first. Private farmland: permission needed.
src: Moorhead Daily News, 24 Nov 1916, p. 4, "Hunt for Hidden Treasure on Morken Township Farm" (newspapers.com 1191726560)
